owner.occupation: Food technologist at a polytechnic lab

world.bio: I'm a food technologist at a polytechnic food lab in Singapore. My specialty is retort-pouch sauces. On weekends I experiment with sambal, trying to make it survive a year on a shelf without losing its aroma or going dark. Planning a hiking trip to Taiwan and learning the erhu from my grandmother.
skills_assets: Pilot-scale retort equipment: a Steriflow lab retort for pouches
Food safety training: HACCP, thermal process validation, pH and water activity testing
Access to the polytechnic's pilot plant and sensory testing room
Sambal recipes passed down by her grandmother
Contacts at SFA and local food SMEs

projects.name: Shelf-stable sambal
projects.text: Trying to make a belacan-based sambal survive 12 months at room temperature in a retort pouch. First two trials darkened and lost the shrimp aroma. Third trial used lower retort temperature and added a little tamarind for pH. Still running accelerated shelf-life tests.

projects.name: Industry grant
projects.text: My industry grant requires a commercial partner with a real product by March. I've spoken to two food SMEs, but neither had a product ready. If I can't find one, I'll have to return a portion of the funding.

projects.name: BTO flat renovation
projects.text: Our BTO flat keys came in August; we're renovating. Kitchen cabinets delayed by three weeks.

notes.text: Trial 3 sambal came out of the retort. Colour is better, a deep red. Aroma still a bit flat. Will test shelf life at 35°C for a month.
Grant officer emailed to remind me about the partner requirement. She asked if I have a name. I said 'in progress'. It is not in progress.
Spent the afternoon at a hawker centre taste-testing sambal stalls. One had a belacan so fragrant I stood there like an idiot. Asked how long it keeps; the auntie laughed: 'one day lah, finish it'.
Erhu lesson with Ah Ma. She said my bowing was too stiff. She did a demonstration and it sounded like a woman crying. I almost cried.
BTO contractor said the kitchen cabinets will be delayed again. We've been eating takeout for three weeks.
Finished planning the Taiwan hike: Alishan, Yushan. Booked leave for early November.
The polytechnic's pilot plant is booked solid with students. I've only got Tuesday afternoons for my sambal. Annoying.
Reading the literature on Maillard browning in retort pouches. Thought: maybe add a bit of ascorbic acid to slow darkening. Will try in trial 4.
National Day fireworks from the flat balcony. Not the BTO one yet, my parents' place. Ah Ma fell asleep on the sofa.
Water activity of trial 3 is 0.89. Need lower or add more preservatives. Not happy.

messages.text: Officer: Dr. Tan, have you identified your commercial partner? Me: I'm in discussions. Officer: The deadline is March. Me: I know.
Ravi: Still stuck on the partner thing? Me: Yes. Ravi: The old industry day list is on the shared drive. Me: Those were all big companies. Ravi: Try the smaller ones.
Ah Ma: Mei Ling, come for dinner. Me: I'll bring the sambal. Ah Ma: Don't bring failed sambal.
Contractor: Cabinets arrive in three weeks. Me: That's what you said last time. Contractor: Supplier delay.
Friend: Alishan sunrise is amazing. Me: Can't wait. Friend: Bring a jacket.

relations.about: Her grandmother, teaches erhu, great sambal maker

constraints: Pilot plant access: Tuesday afternoons only
Grant terms: partner must be a registered local company
Cannot use equipment for commercial production at scale
sensitive: Worried about returning part of the grant
Her lab director doesn't know she hasn't found a partner
